title: These 5 AI Stocks Print Cash. The Rest Are Burning It.
creator: MarketBeat
source_note: Guest Joseph Hogue (Let's Talk Money). Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names ('Joseph Hog', 'Palenter/Palunteer' for Palantir, 'Crest' for interim CEO Colette Kress, 'Wang' for Jensen Huang).
summary: MarketBeat hosts guest Joseph Hogue, who frames the AI sell-off as the longest in years: the Global X AIQ ETF is down about 20% over 119 days since its peak, versus 14% in 18 days in 2024 and 26% in 35 days in 2025. He calls it a perfect storm - election worries about a Congress-driven data-centre slowdown, then the Nvidia CEO drama and politics - but says the long-term growth story is intact, with Nvidia guiding 75% revenue growth and a $2.5 trillion backlog and Gartner projecting about 47% growth in global AI capital investment. His screen of 40 AI names plots revenue growth against free-cash-flow margin, and his five 'cash-flow kings' fell only about 15% on average versus 30-40% for other AI darlings. Nvidia (NVDA, BUY, fair value about 2x current): ~96% revenue growth, ~80% free-cash-flow margin, 10-15x forward earnings versus ~30x historically; key-man risk acknowledged. Broadcom (AVGO, BUY, fair value $525, ~70% upside): 63-65% revenue growth, over 80% free-cash-flow margin, custom silicon plus networking locking customers in. Palantir (PLTR, BUY): 91% revenue growth, ~101% free-cash-flow margin - the highest of his 40-stock screen - with a PEG under 1 versus 3-5x historically. Arista Networks (ANET, BUY first tracked): networking is a data-centre bottleneck Arista does better than almost anyone, ~50% growth and 60% free-cash-flow margin. Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM, BUY first tracked): near-monopoly in advanced chip manufacturing, about 55% of global semiconductors and 90%+ of high-performance AI chips, still up about 22% for the year.
